title: [rtl,pmp] Allow all accesses to Debug Module in debug mode
body:
The RISC-V Debug Specification ([current release 1.0.0-rc4](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-debug-spec/releases/tag/1.0.0-rc4)) in Section A.2 states that the PMP must not disallow accesses to addresses of the Debug Module when the hart is in debug mode, regardless of how the PMP is configured.  This commit changes the PMP accordingly.

This PR doesn't contain the verification, which is tracked by #2233.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[controller] Add assertion on pipeline flush when entering debug mode

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

[rtl,pmp] Allow all accesses to Debug Module in debug mode

The RISC-V Debug Specification (current release 1.0.0-rc4) in Section
A.2 states that the PMP must not disallow accesses to addresses of the
Debug Module when the hart is in debug mode, regardless of how the PMP
is configured.  This commit changes the PMP accordingly.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Kurth <adk@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [dv] Verify access to Debug Module in debug mode even if disallowed by PMP
resolved_issues.body:
Verify the feature implemented in #2232; specific tasks are:
- [ ] (P1) Minimal smoke test that verifies the feature works (i.e., read, write, and fetch a couple of addresses in the Debug Module address space while debug mode is enabled but the PMP doesn't allow the accesses).
- [ ] (P2) Extensive testing that verifies the feature cannot be used for accesses outside the Debug Module address space that are disallowed by the PMP.
- [ ] (P3) Extensive testing that verifies the feature works (close coverage over all addressing cases cross access types cross relevant states).

problem_statement: The Physical Memory Protection (PMP) logic in Ibex still rejects accesses to the RISC-V Debug Module address range even when the processor core is already in debug mode. If the active PMP rules would normally deny the access, a load, store, or instruction fetch to an address inside the Debug Module range can incorrectly raise a PMP access error. The correct behavior is that, while debug mode is active, PMP must allow loads, stores, and instruction fetches within the Debug Module address range even when those same accesses would otherwise be blocked by PMP. At the same time, accesses outside the Debug Module address range must continue to follow normal PMP checks and must still fault when PMP denies them. This bug affects the PMP permission-check path for debug-mode accesses and is triggered when the core, while in debug mode, accesses an address in the Debug Module range under PMP rules that would otherwise deny the access.
